issues.description: The UML in the problem statement specifies addGuestStudents(int): void (no return value), but the solution implementation declares addGuestStudents(int) returning boolean. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected method signature and return behavior and may cause tests or grading code that expect a void method to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the addGuestStudents method signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the solution to match the UML/problem statement by changing the method to public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and remove the boolean return (just update the internal numberOfGuestStudents), or (B) update the problem statement/UML to indicate a boolean return and clarify the return semantics (e.g., return true on success, false on invalid input). Prefer option A if the intent is a simple mutator with no return value.
